tickets.title: Third Avenue L stop closure pilot proposal
tickets.summary: A public speaker who analyzed MTA trip data said the Third Avenue L stop serves only about 5% of riders getting on or off, and that closing it would save New Yorkers roughly 1,800 hours a day. He said it is not a transfer station and not wheelchair accessible, and that walking time for riders would increase by about 2 minutes on average. Action: Refer the proposal to the transportation committee and ask the district office to explore a pilot stop closure with the MTA.

tickets.title: Delivery worker e-bike storage on 11th Street
tickets.summary: Over 100 electric bikes used by food delivery workers are stored on sidewalks and in the street around 11th Street, obstructing businesses, landlords, and residents, with some businesses closing. Elected officials and the district manager said the block lacks legal parking or corral space, and a planned police enforcement action on October 7 would confiscate improperly parked bikes. Speakers asked for multilingual warnings, tagging instead of seizure, and help finding a fenced site for the workers. Action: Ask the precinct and city agencies to provide multilingual notice before enforcement, consider tagging as an alternative, and help identify a legal storage site.

tickets.title: Drug activity and lighting in Seward Park
tickets.summary: Residents and park users reported increased drug use and homelessness in Seward Park, and the Lower East Side Ecology Center said a bathroom next to its building is frequented by drug users. A speaker also noted dark spots in the park that allow drug use to go unseen. The district manager said police are now stationed there and that outreach providers work in the area, and a participant asked whether mobile crisis teams could be expanded to reduce drug use. Action: Ask the 7th Precinct and Parks Department to address the drug activity and lighting, and ask the city to consider expanding mobile crisis response in the park.

tickets.title: Transportation costs to 125th Street office
tickets.summary: A community member asked whether MTA cards or OMNY alternatives could offset transit costs for residents traveling to the new immigrant welcome center on 125th Street, noting the trip can take an hour with multiple transfers. The elected official's staffer said the question would be raised with the office. Action: Ask the Manhattan Borough President's office to consider transportation cost support for residents who need to reach the uptown immigrant center.

tickets.title: Essex Market RFP postponement and community market terms
tickets.summary: The land use and economic development committees reviewed the EDC request for proposals for Essex Market and found EDC could not confirm that the board's two resolutions were included. The RFP was due to go out at the end of the month, and the committees asked EDC to postpone issuance. Action: Hold a follow-up meeting with EDC this week to confirm the resolutions are reflected and request that the RFP be postponed until terms are clarified.

tickets.title: Manhattan Bridge exit safety concerns letter
tickets.summary: The transportation committee reported that a recent crash and death at the foot of Manhattan Bridge prompted renewed concerns about the exits. A letter restating the board's prior resolutions was sent to the mayor and DOT. Action: Follow up with the mayor and DOT to request a response on the Manhattan Bridge exit concerns.

tickets.title: Canal Street redesign project update request
tickets.summary: The board has not received an update on the Canal Street redesign project since January, so the transportation committee included a request for one in its letter to the mayor and DOT. Action: Obtain a current status update on the Canal Street redesign from DOT and report it to the board.

tickets.title: Cross-town bus and parking equity study
tickets.summary: The transportation committee met with the Independent Budget Office to look at transportation equity in the district and narrowed about ten research ideas to three. The top priorities included cross-town bus service and neighborhood parking locations. Action: Follow up with the Independent Budget Office on the cross-town bus and neighborhood parking research requests.

tickets.title: Free public restroom pilot access and resolution
tickets.summary: The city is installing 17 free public restrooms citywide as a one-year pilot, with two in this district. The transportation committee raised concerns about access, who may use the restrooms, and emergency calls. Action: Vote on a resolution next month setting out the board's requests for access and operation during the pilot period.

tickets.title: Congestion pricing FDR traffic impact follow-up
tickets.summary: A committee member asked whether the congestion pricing traffic increase predicted for the FDR in the air quality report actually occurred and whether reporting is planned. The transportation committee said it could follow up on this question. Action: Ask MTA or DOT whether the predicted FDR congestion impact materialized and whether they will report on it to the board.

tickets.title: Ticket vending reform in Battery Park
tickets.summary: A council office reintroduced a bill to reform ticket vending in Battery Park, which affects New Yorkers and tourists, and held a press conference with community board members and other organizations. The office is discussing a hearing on the issue in the fall. Action: Track the scheduled council hearing and report back to the board on the outcome.

tickets.title: NYCHA residents' food access and communication access
tickets.summary: A public speaker described NYCHA residents struggling with lack of food, water, and basic necessities, and asked how the community can help. A hard-of-hearing speaker said communication access, including interpreters and sign language, is essential for deaf residents. Action: Refer the food access and communication access concerns to the district office and relevant city agencies for follow-up.

tickets.title: Proposed indoor roller skating facility on East River Pier
tickets.location_raw: East River Pier across from the Katherine Slip Mall
tickets.summary: A speaker proposed a 300,000 square foot multi-use building with indoor roller skating on the East River Pier, with $8 admission and projected 250 to 400 direct jobs. The proposal responds to the loss of indoor skating rinks in New York City. Action: Ask the district office to review the proposal and advise the speaker on the appropriate city process for using pier space.

tickets.title: Mobile voting option for CEC elections
tickets.summary: A resolution supports piloting a mobile-first voting option for Community Education Council elections, because turnout has been around 2% and many households rely only on smartphones. Speakers asked that outreach make clear that voting is for school participation and that immigrant families' data and status will be protected. Action: Vote on the resolution and send it to the Department of Education urging a mobile voting pilot and expanded multilingual outreach.

tickets.title: August SLA denial for 11 Allen Street
tickets.summary: The board voted to recommend denial of an SLA application for 11 Allen Street from the operator of Time Again, which is at a location with past problems, and the vote passed. Committee members noted the area is saturated and that the committee had proposed stipulations limiting hours and DJs. Because the board's denial is only a recommendation, the State Liquor Authority could still approve the license without stipulations if the community does not attend. Action: Organize community members to attend the SLA hearing and ask elected officials to support the denial.

tickets.title: Correcting August SLA resolution wording
tickets.summary: The SLA committee chair reported two clerical errors in the August resolutions, for item 3 Cozy Cafe and item 10 Soft Hours Tea House. Both resolutions said the board recommends denial of a full on-premises license when they should say denial of a beer and wine license unless stipulations are agreed to. Action: Correct the August resolution language to reflect a beer and wine license for both items and circulate the corrected text.

tickets.title: Bylaws attendance and removal process revision
tickets.summary: The bylaws committee presented proposed changes to attendance procedures, adding an early letter and executive committee meeting after excess absences and removing attendance from the general removal process. The proposal also requires public members to follow conflict of interest policies. A member noted the executive committee and board chair both make a recommendation, which the committee may need to clarify. Action: Vote on the proposed bylaws changes at the October full board meeting with the required 28-day notice.

tickets.title: Board trainings on SLA and Robert's Rules
tickets.summary: The board chair announced planned trainings on SLA procedures, Robert's Rules, and office procedures, with dates to be announced. The chair asked members to email requests for specific training topics or questions. Action: Schedule the SLA, Robert's Rules, and office procedures trainings and report the dates to the board.

tickets.title: District needs and budget priority rankings
tickets.summary: The district manager said the board will vote in October on its district needs statement and ranked expense and capital priorities for each city agency. The board's top stated need is affordable housing, but the draft city housing plan allocates only about 25% of its roughly 7,000 planned units to affordable housing. Action: Hold committee votes on district needs and budget priorities in October and rank priorities by agency.

tickets.title: East River Park stewardship facility construction delay
tickets.summary: The parks committee learned that construction of the new facility that will house the Lower East Side Ecology Center and stewardship programs is delayed by procurement challenges. The Parks Department offered to return in October with more detail on the delay and on interim support for park stewardship. Action: Ask the Parks Department to return in October with the procurement details, revised timeline, and interim stewardship support plan.
